DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Position [L4]:** The KJV says the child's conception and begetting came from the Holy Ghost, through a virgin, with no man involved. By "biological father" I mean a male whose seed begot the child. Joseph was husband and legal guardian, and he was never that.

---

## 1. Matthew's genealogy stops begetting at Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". The chain proceeds "begat... begat" down to Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The verb "begat" is *gennaō* (G1080, to beget). In verse 16 the pattern changes. Joseph is called "the husband of Mary", not the begetter of Jesus. The relative "of whom" is *ex hēs*, "out of whom", in the feminine singular. It points only to Mary, and the birth is traced to her alone.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20 uses the same root for what happened in Mary: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost". The Greek is *gennēthen*, "begotten/conceived". The begetting is located "in her" and sourced "of the Holy Ghost".

**[L4]** From the broken "begat" chain in Matthew 1:16 and the feminine "of whom", the genealogy gives Joseph a legal and husbandly place, not a begetting one.

## 2. The conception is sourced from the Holy Ghost

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** "Of" is *ek*, "out of", a word of source. The phrase is *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Spirit". The text names the source of the child.

**[L3]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." Here *episkiasei* means "shall overshadow". The "therefore" ties the child's being called the Son of God to this act.

**[L3]** Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me". The Greek *katērtisō* means "fitted, made ready". The body is said to be prepared, not begotten by a man.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 give the Holy Ghost as the source with *ek*. Luke 1:35 makes the Son-of-God status follow from that act ("therefore"). Together they exclude a male contributor, since a second source would leave the "of the Holy Ghost" statement incomplete.

## 3. The mother was a virgin who knew no man

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph". **[L2]** *Parthenos* (G3933) means a virgin, an unmarried girl without sexual experience.

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" **[L2]** *Ginōskō* (G1097, to know) is the word used of sexual union, and *andra* (G435) means a male human.

**[L3]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived". The verb "knew" carries conception there, so "I know not a man" speaks of the means.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son". The same verb *ginōskō* is used. Joseph did not know her until after the birth.

**[L3]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son". **[L2]** The Hebrew word is *almah* (H5959), and the KJV renders it "virgin". It is a sign the Lord "himself shall give", and it is fulfilled in Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son".

**[L4]** Luke 1:34 is a question about means, and Luke 1:35 answers it with the Holy Ghost, not with a man. The prophecy (Isaiah 7:14), its fulfilment (Matthew 1:23) and Matthew 1:25 all state the virgin conception and birth. A virgin conception leaves no room for a male begetter.

## 4. Joseph's fatherhood is "supposed", not biological

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". **[L2]** *Enomizeto* (G3543) means "was thought, reckoned". Luke says it was supposed, and the verse sets the supposition apart from the fact.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Joseph knew the child was not his and acted on that knowledge. Matthew 1:20 corrects him: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "Thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." **[L3]** The child answers in Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" He moves the word "father" from Joseph to God.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:21 ("thou shalt call his name JESUS") and 1:25 ("he called his name JESUS") give Joseph the naming and the guardianship of a husband. The "father" in Luke 2:48 is the supposed father of Luke 3:23, and Luke 2:49 corrects it.

## 5. Pre-empting the descent from David

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh". **[L1]** Luke 1:32: "the throne of his father David".

**[L3]** "Father" is used of a forefather in Luke 1:73: "The oath which he sware to our father Abraham". **[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman".

**[L2]** *Genomenou* (G1096, made, come to be) is the verb in Romans 1:3 and Galatians 4:4. *Ek* in Romans 1:3 gives the line of descent, and Galatians 4:4 gives the woman as the one through whom he came to be.

**[L4]** Luke 1:73 shows "father" naming an ancestor. Romans 1:3 and Galatians 4:4 use the same verb, *genomenou*, and trace descent through "a woman". The Davidic descent is carried by the mother's line, and Joseph is not required as begetter.

---

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. Matthew's genealogy breaks the "begat" pattern at Joseph and traces the birth only to Mary. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:16 "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus" with [L2] *ex hēs* (feminine "out of whom") and *gennaō* (to beget), carried by [L3] Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her".
2. The text names the Holy Ghost as the source of the conception. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18 "found with child of the Holy Ghost" with [L2] *ek* (out of, source), carried by [L3] Luke 1:35 "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee... therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee".
3. Mary was a virgin and had known no man. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:34 "seeing I know not a man" with [L2] *ginōskō* (to know sexually), carried by [L3] Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth" and Genesis 4:1.
4. Joseph is called the child's father only by supposition. Footing: [L1] Luke 3:23 "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph" with [L2] *enomizeto* (was reckoned), carried by [L3] Luke 2:49 "my Father's business" and Matthew 1:19-20.
5. The descent from David and the word "father" do not require a male begetter. Footing: [L1] Romans 1:3 "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" with [L2] *genomenou* (made, come to be), carried by [L3] Galatians 4:4 "made of a woman" and Luke 1:73 "our father Abraham".
6. Christ had no biological father. His conception was of the Holy Ghost in a virgin, and Joseph was his supposed father and Mary's husband. Footing: [L4] from links 1 to 5, resting on [L1] Matthew 1:18 and Luke 1:35 and [L2] *ek* (out of, source) and *gennaō* (to beget).

# Link round and answer to the challenger's question

I concede what floats and keep what stands. Where I grant a row, I do not use it against its own words.

## LINK 1 (D1): SUPPORTED

**[L1]** Matthew 1:3: "And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares begat Esrom; and Esrom begat Aram;" Matthew 1:5: "And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse;" Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080, to procreate, "properly, of the father"). In Matthew 1:3 and 1:5 the father is the subject of the active "begat" for the child named. In 1:16 the active "begat" ends at "Joseph". The child Jesus then comes under the passive "was born", with the feminine relative *ex hēs* (out of whom). The pressed rows show Matthew's mother-marker as an addition to a father's active begetting. At 1:16 the father's active verb stops before the child.

**[L3]** Genesis 4:25: "And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son". Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son". Genesis 4:25 states the father's knowing in the same verse as the birth. Matthew 1:25 states the opposite of Joseph. Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." I grant that Joseph is addressed as "son of David". The angel pairs that address with commands to take Mary and to call the name (Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS").

**[L4]** Matthew 1:3 and 1:5 (active father-begetting), Matthew 1:16 (active verb stops at Joseph, passive "was born" with *ex hēs*) and Matthew 1:25 together show that Joseph holds the husband's office, addressed as "son of David" with commands to take and to name. The child is traced to Mary, not to his begetting.

## LINK 2 (D2): SUPPORTED

**[L1]** 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God". John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." Acts 1:8: "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you". Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them". Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David". 1 Chronicles 28:6: "for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."

**[L2]** I grant *gennaō* with *ek* (out of) God in 1 John 5:1, and I grant *eperchomai* (G1904, to come upon, to influence) and *episkiazō* (G1982, to overshadow, to invest with influence) as power and presence. The objects differ. In 1 John 5:1 the one begotten of God is a person who "believeth". In Matthew 1:20 the object is "that which is conceived in her", the content of the womb. In Matthew 1:18 the one found "with child" is "of the Holy Ghost".

**[L3]** John 3:6 sets the flesh-birth and the Spirit-birth as two origins of two things. In 1 John 5:1 the believer already has a flesh-birth and receives the Spirit-birth after it. Matthew 1:18 puts the "with child" itself under "of the Holy Ghost". Luke 1:35 places the verbs of power on Mary as the answer to "How shall this be?" in Luke 1:34. In Luke 1:35 the "therefore also" follows in the same verse as "shall come upon thee... shall overshadow thee", so the title "Son of God" is tied to that act. In 1 Chronicles 28:6 the stated ground of the title is "I have chosen him". In Luke 1:35 the stated ground is the Holy Ghost's coming. Psalms 2:7 is applied in Acts 13:33 to "he hath raised up Jesus again" and in Hebrews 5:5 to the high priesthood, so it is not the ground Luke 1:35 gives.

**[VOID (pkgBAR): a barred move struck by the system. The press this answered counts as unanswered.] Solomon's title rests on choice and Jesus' on the overshadowing.

**Hebrews 10:5, 2:14, 2:17.** Hebrews 10:5 reads "a body hast thou prepared me [or, thou hast fitted me]", so the body is prepared by the one addressed. Hebrews 2:14 reads "Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same". Hebrews 2:17 reads "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren". **[L4]** The likeness these verses state is the sharing of "flesh and blood", the thing taken. Luke 1:35 gives the source of that flesh and blood as "that holy thing which shall be born of thee", so Mary supplies the flesh and blood that Hebrews 2:14 says he took. The likeness is fully carried by the mother's flesh and blood.

## LINK 3 (D3): SUPPORTED

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:24: "and took unto him his wife". Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son". I accept the challenger's ordering of the verses.

**[L3]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived". Deuteronomy 22:24: "he hath humbled his neighbour's wife". Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son". Matthew 1:19 names "Joseph her husband" within the espousal, and I grant that. The finding of the child, "before they came together" (1:18), comes before the taking (1:24). The abstinence, "knew her not till" (1:25), runs from the taking to the birth. So the interval for the Genesis 4:1 means, knowing, is closed on both sides by the challenger's own ordering.

**[L2]** *ginōskō* (G1097, to know, here of union) in Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:25. *Parthenos* (G3933, virgin) in Luke 1:27.

**[L4]** Luke 1:34 asks how, and Luke 1:35 answers with the Holy Ghost. With Matthew 1:18 and 1:25, the answer is the Holy Ghost's coming, placed before the coming together and held until the birth.

**Isaiah 7:16 and 8:3.** Isaiah 7:14 reads "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive". The Hebrew *almah* (H5959) stands behind the KJV's "virgin". Isaiah 8:3 reads "I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. Then said the LORD to me, Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz." It has a different woman, "the prophetess", a different name, "Mahershalalhashbaz", and the margin "went: Heb. approached". Isaiah 7:14 names "Immanuel". Isaiah 8:8 says "thy land, O Immanuel". Matthew 1:22-23 says "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled", and it quotes "Behold, a virgin shall be with child".

## LINK 4 (D4, Matthew 1:19): PARTLY CONCEDED, NARROWED

I concede the words "Joseph knew the child was not his". Matthew 1:19 states an intent and two grounds: "being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Those words carry Joseph's justice and his purpose.

What I keep stands on Matthew 1:18-20. **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." **[L2]** *enthymeomai* (G1760, to ponder) is the verb of "he thought on these things", so the angel's word comes to Joseph in the midst of his pondering. *gar* (for, G1063) gives the ground of the command, and the ground clause is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Spirit). **[L3]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child". **[L4]** The ground the angel gives for taking Mary is "of the Holy Ghost", and it is told to Joseph by the angel in answer to a purpose formed when she was "found with child... before they came together". The origin reaches Joseph as news from the angel.

## LINK 5 (D4, Luke 2:49): SUPPORTED AS NARROWED

I grant Luke 2:48 "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing", Luke 2:51 "and was subject unto them", and Luke 2:41 "his parents went to Jerusalem every year". Joseph is father in the household. **[L1]** Luke 3:23 qualifies the sonship: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". **[L2]** *nomizō* (G3543, to reckon, from *nomos*, law or custom): the challenger gives *enomizeto* as reckoning by law or usage, as in Acts 16:13 "where prayer was wont to be made". I accept this meaning. A sonship reckoned by law or custom is a reckoning, and the pressed row calls it "supposed". **[L3]** Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers" names a registry. That registry is the legal reckoning I rest on in the answer below, and I do not use it as the begetting.

**[L4]** The father-title for Joseph in Luke 2:48 and Luke 2:41 is the household and legal title, and Luke 3:23 sets it under "supposed". I do not claim Luke 2:49 withdraws the title from Joseph. Luke 2:49, "my Father's business", sets the Father beside him.

## LINK 6 (D5): PARTLY CONCEDED, NARROWED

I concede "The Davidic descent is carried by the mother's line." Luke 1:27 attaches "of the house of David" to Joseph, and Luke 2:4 says "because he was of the house and lineage of David" of Joseph. Luke 1:36, "thy cousin Elisabeth", and Luke 1:5, "his wife [was] of the daughters of Aaron", I do not rest on.

What I keep is narrower. **[L1]** Acts 2:30: "Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne". **[L2]** *osphys* (G3751, loins): the "his" is David, the one to whom God "had sworn with an oath", so the loins are David's. **[L3]** Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." The loins phrase reaches across generations, since the one yet "in the loins" of his father is a descendant carried in the ancestor's body. Romans 1:3 gives "made of the seed of David according to the flesh", the seed of David. Luke 1:73 uses "our father Abraham" as forefather.

**[L4]** Acts 2:30 and Romans 1:3 trace the flesh to David as ancestor, and Hebrews 7:10 shows the loins language covering many generations at once. These texts carry a descent from David across generations. They are footed on the ancestor, and each is complete without a named begetter in Joseph's place.

I grant that Job 14:1, "Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days", Matthew 11:11, "Among them that are born of women", and Luke 1:13, "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son", show "of a woman" said of men with fathers. I do not rest the source of Christ's origin on "made of a woman" in Galatians 4:4.

## LINK 7 (D6, keystone): SUPPORTED

**[L1]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph." These are spoken by Philip and by the crowd, and John 6:42 is a challenge to "I came down from heaven". **[L3]** Luke 3:23 labels this reckoning "as was supposed". **[L4]** John 6:42 and John 1:45 report the common reckoning that Luke 3:23 calls supposed. The narrator of Luke 3:23 and of Matthew 1:18 speaks in his own voice, and the speakers in John 6:42 and John 1:45 speak as the crowd and as Philip.

Links 1 to 5 carry Matthew 1:18 and 1:20, Luke 1:35 and the *ek* of source. Link 6 now carries only what is kept above.

## Answer to the question on Hebrews 7:14

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda". **[L3]** Numbers 1:2: "by the house of their fathers". Luke 2:4: Joseph "was of the house and lineage of David". I grant that the registered house is Joseph's. The reckoning came by his taking Mary (Matthew 1:20, 1:24) and by his naming the child (Matthew 1:21, "thou shalt call his name JESUS"; Matthew 1:25, "he called his name JESUS"). **[L2]** *paralambanō* (G3880, to receive near, to associate with oneself) is the verb of "take unto thee" in Matthew 1:20. **[L4]** Hebrews 7:14 says "sprang out of Juda", and the registry reckons that to Joseph's house. The rows that place Joseph in that house give him a taking and a naming (*paralambanō*, Matthew 1:21, 1:25), and the source of the conceived child they give is "of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20).

## DECLARED CHAIN (as kept)

1. Matthew 1:16's active "begat" stops at Joseph, and Jesus is "of whom was born", out of Mary. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:3, 1:5, 1:16 with [L2] *gennaō* and *ex hēs*, carried by [L3] Matthew 1:25 and Genesis 4:25.
2. The Holy Ghost is the stated source of what was conceived. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 with [L2] *ek* and *gar*, carried by [L3] Luke 1:35 and John 3:6.
3. The conception was found before the coming together, and Matthew 1:25 bounds the abstinence after it. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18, 1:24, 1:25 with [L2] *ginōskō*, carried by [L3] Luke 1:34-35 and Isaiah 7:14.
4. Joseph is father by household and legal reckoning, "as was supposed". Footing: [L1] Luke 3:23 with [L2] *nomizō*, carried by [L3] Numbers 1:18 and Matthew 1:21, 1:25.
5. The loins and seed texts trace the flesh to David as ancestor across generations. Footing: [L1] Acts 2:30 with [L2] *osphys*, carried by [L3] Hebrews 7:10.
6. Christ had no biological father. His conception was of the Holy Ghost, and Joseph was his father by legal reckoning. Footing: [L4] from links 1 to 5, on [L1] Matthew 1:18 and Luke 1:35 and [L2] *ek*.

# LINK ROUND

## LINK 1: SUPPORTED

**Footing.**
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080, to procreate, properly of the father, by extension of the mother) stands in both clauses. The first is active ("begat") and governs Joseph. The second is passive ("was born") and is tied to the feminine relative "of whom."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]."
- **[L4]** Matthew 1:2 uses the active "begat" of fathers. Matthew 1:20 puts the same verb in the passive with its source "of the Holy Ghost." So Matthew 1:16 gives Joseph the relation "husband of Mary" and gives the child's birth to "whom," Mary.

**Answers to the pressed verses.**
- Matthew 1:3 "And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar" and Matthew 1:5 "And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth". I grant that "of" plus a mother's name stands beside a begetting father in those verses. At Matthew 1:16 the active "begat" ends at Joseph ("Jacob begat Joseph"). The clause about Jesus is passive with the feminine "of whom."
- Genesis 4:25 "And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son". I grant that the birth is told with the husband's knowing there. Matthew 1:25 tells the birth with the opposite: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- Matthew 1:20 "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife". I grant that Joseph is named "son of David" and Mary "thy wife." The same verse gives the ground for his not fearing: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." *gennaō* (G1080) with its source "of the Holy Ghost" is the begetting the verse states. Matthew 1:18 repeats it: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- Matthew 1:24 "and took unto him his wife". I grant that *paralambanō* (G3880, to receive near) is the coming together of Matthew 1:18.
- Matthew 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son". I grant that *heōs* (G2193, until) runs from the taking to the birth. The sources of the conceiving are stated in Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 as the Holy Ghost, not Joseph.

## LINK 2: SUPPORTED

**Footing.**
- **[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080) with "of thee" gives the source as the mother. *dynamis* (G1411, power) is the cause stated in the same verse.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The verse that answers this question is the one that carries "therefore also."
- **[L4]** The cause is stated inside Luke 1:35 itself: the Holy Ghost coming and the power overshadowing. The "therefore also" is joined to that cause in the same sentence.

**Answers to the pressed verses.**
- Luke 1:32 "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David". I grant that *kaleō* (G2564, to call) is the verb in both verses and that the title is given before the question. Luke 1:35 gives the ground of the title with "therefore also," so its ground is stated there.
- 1 Chronicles 28:6 "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father". The ground there is *bachar* (H977, to choose) of a son who is already "Solomon thy son." Luke 1:35's ground is the coming of the Holy Ghost, and its subject is "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
